paragraphs: Many years before, Swamiji went to see a great and very holy sage in India. Their conversation turned to sacred books: the Vedas, the Bible, the Koran, and scriptures in general.

As the talk was ending, the sage asked Swamiji to pick up a book lying on the table. Among other things, it gave a forecast of how much rain would fall that year. The sage asked him to read it, and Swamiji read aloud the expected rainfall.

Then came an odd request: squeeze the book. Swamiji did. The sage smiled and pointed out that not one drop of water had come out of it. Until the water actually falls, he explained, all you have is words on paper. Religion is the same. Until it leads you to realise God for yourself, it is of no real use.
A person who only reads about religion, the sage said, is like the donkey in the old fable. It carried a heavy load of sugar on its back all day, yet never once knew how sweet it was.
learn: Reading about something is not the same as living it, whether it is faith, fitness or kindness. Information is the forecast; experience is the rain. Ask yourself which of your beliefs you have actually tasted.
